newsitem.title: UK: Anglian sees no problems with leakage targets.
newsitem.headline: Anglian sees no problems with leakage targets.

text.p: British water and sewerage company Anglian Water plc does not expect any problems in meeting targets to cut leakage which are likely to be set by the new Labour government, John Green, head of Anglian Water Services, told Reuters Financial Television.

"Clearly in Anglian, with leakage at 11.8 percent, we don't believe that manadatory leakage targets are going to be a problem for us," Green said in an interview which will be broadcast on RFTV's Inside Equities at 1045 GMT.
Anglian has one of the lowest leakage rates of Britain's water and sewerage companies.

Deputy prime minister John Prescott called a "crisis summit" on water earlier this month as the country faces a severe drought and vowed to introduce mandatory leakage targets for the companies to cut the estimated 800 million gallons which leaks out of pipes daily.

Labour has also said it will levy a one-off tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities and Green said the company did not believe it was a fair tax, "but we do recognise the government has a mandate."
Green said Anglian felt if the tax were levied, it should be "fed back into the anglian region...to improve job prospects within our operating area."
He said that if the tax were deemed to be illegal, "our shareholders would expect us to mount a legal challenge".
Other companies which might be covered by the proposed tax have indicated that they might look at the possibility of legal challenges.
